items.title: Verstappen wins as Antonelli clinches the title
items.summary: Max Verstappen recovered from a grid penalty to win, keeping Lewis Hamilton at bay. Kimi Antonelli's podium secured his maiden Drivers' Championship. Hamilton had taken Ferrari's first pole of 2026 with a 1m 16.514s Q3 lap.
items.why_it_matters: The title is decided and Ferrari lost a race they were positioned to win; this is the post-race baseline for Sao Paulo.

sources.label: Formula1.com: Verstappen on his winning move

items.title: Opening-lap clash leaves Ferrari with P2 and P4
items.summary: Fred Vasseur said Ferrari should have won after the intra-team opening-lap clash and called it 'a matter of respect'. Leclerc conceded he deserved a penalty and Hamilton expects 'some serious talks'.
items.why_it_matters: Team harmony is the main Ferrari storyline; these are team and driver accounts, not an official finding beyond the stewards' decision.

items.title: Piastri, Gasly and Colapinto lose finishing positions
items.summary: Oscar Piastri lost P7 for a 10-second penalty for causing a collision with Arvid Lindblad. Pierre Gasly (P10) and Franco Colapinto (P8) were separately penalised for yellow-flag infringements and lost their finishes; The Race reports Alpine lost all its Mexican GP points.
items.why_it_matters: Use the amended classification, not the chequered-flag order, when quoting points or form.

items.title: Honda-powered Aston Martin double retirement after five laps
items.summary: One AMR26 retired in the pits after five laps while the other stopped on track at the same time. Formula1.com calls it perhaps the team's most disappointing weekend of 2026.
items.why_it_matters: A reliability and Honda power-unit talking point heading into Sao Paulo; the cause is covered in the linked report.
